chunks: Ali ibn Ja'far narrated from Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) who said:
I asked him about a man who took a bird from Mecca until he brought it to Kufa; what should he do? He said: 'He should return it to Mecca, and if it dies, he should give its price in charity.'

key_terms.الْكُوفَةَ: Kufa (a major city in Iraq, often used as a reference point for travel from Mecca)
key_terms.طَيْر: Bird (specifically a bird brought for food or sacrifice)
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Mecca (the holy city and center of Hajj rituals)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who brings a bird from Mecca to Kufa?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific penalty for a pilgrim who transports a hunted animal out of the Miqat boundary, requiring its return to Mecca to maintain the sanctity of the Haram. If the animal perishes during transit, the pilgrim must pay its value as charity, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential principle of compensating for the loss of the sacred object itself. This highlights the strict preservation of the Haram's boundaries and the tangible consequences of violating ihram restrictions.
